findings.claim: The specified statistical method cannot estimate within-question variation from the proposed singleton runs.
findings.evidence: The plan specifies within-question paired bootstrap and a pooled within-question variance floor, while X1 and X2 at lines 233–234 run each question once per arm. evidence/validation-2026-11-07-RESULT.md:34–44 describes the existing method using repeated runs and warns about collapsed intervals; line 127 proposes pooling within-question variation, which singleton cells cannot supply.
findings.fix: Define a method valid for the proposed sampling design, including the source of the variance floor and the equivalence calculation, before approving the experiments and budget.

findings.claim: The new judgment rules are not connected to the catalog engine that must enforce and record them.
findings.evidence: scripts/catalog_core.py:1847–1849 accepts only better/same/worse and a fixed 1.5 cost threshold. Lines 2062–2111 derive and validate outcomes from a point cost ratio, without confidence intervals or separate equivalent/undetermined states. The plan changes these distinctions but only schedules a statistics module and continues claiming that record-tasting enforces consistent verdicts.
findings.fix: Add an explicit mapping from the new statistical results to catalog judgments, update validation where necessary, and preserve compatibility with historical records.

findings.claim: The proposed policy invokes review after implementation, although deep review must happen before implementation.
findings.evidence: The replacement policy says to use oaw-review after making changes. The deep workflow at line 108 instead requires planning and EGM review before implementation. scripts/oaw_mode.py:115–141 normally examines changes already present in the working tree.
findings.fix: Specify when planned work is classified before implementation and when completed changes receive code review. Include an E2E case proving that deep implementation does not begin before plan review.

findings.claim: Keeping the current triggers does not implement the stated trigger for new design documents generally.
findings.evidence: scripts/oaw_mode.py:246–249 recognizes added Markdown only under docs/designs/ or with a filename matching design*.md. An added docs/plans/v2.0.1-execution.md is classified as light by the current classifier, despite being a new implementation plan.
findings.fix: Either describe the actual restricted trigger or explicitly expand it and add fixtures for the repository's plan paths. Distinguish any expanded trigger from the trigger evaluated in V7.

findings.claim: The user-facing commands have no specified delivery path into an installed project.
findings.evidence: scripts/oaw.py:2 explicitly says this CLI remains in the framework checkout. Its source_files mapping at lines 277–285 installs project helpers, but neither oaw.py nor catalog.py. The payload changes listed in the plan add code_index.py, leaving the advertised project-relative add/list/remove commands and /oaw-add backend unresolved.
findings.fix: Specify either an installed management launcher with its dependencies or commands run from the framework checkout with an explicit project target. Test the documented flow from a separately installed project.

findings.claim: The 'only A B C' choice needs an installation mode that the current installer does not provide.
findings.evidence: scripts/oaw.py:277–279 always includes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and OAW helpers, even with an empty bundled-skill selection. doctor at lines 745–778 requires OAW policy and helpers. Wrapping the existing catalog therefore does not provide the promised management-only installation.
findings.fix: Add a concrete management-only installation contract, including its manifest, doctor behavior and handling of existing OAW versus project-owned policy. Test this choice in both a clean project and an existing OAW installation.

findings.claim: The proposed wrapper cannot install ordinary untested or executable skills through the current catalog absorption path.
findings.evidence: scripts/catalog_core.py:1242–1267 holds executable skills and even static skill text without a behavior A/B. Lines 1268–1284 prohibit installing hooks/MCP servers and hold agents. scripts/catalog.py:1863–1873 installs only components already approved for absorption and rejects bundled-name collisions. W3 promises installation before tasting, executable-component consent and collision choices without scheduling these engine changes.
findings.fix: Define a user-requested installation path separately from promotion into OAW defaults, and explicitly implement the required component and collision handling. Test an untested skill and an ordinary script-bearing skill.

findings.claim: Existing catalog restore points cannot provide the promised rollback for consented hooks and MCP configuration.
findings.evidence: scripts/catalog.py:1407–1420 explicitly excludes host settings and MCP files from build snapshots. Yet W3 permits installing those components and line 192 requires byte-identical restoration after removal.
findings.fix: Specify restoration records for every configuration file the new installer changes, including shared-file edits. Verify that removing B preserves A, C and pre-existing project configuration.

findings.claim: The zero-token installation promise includes semantic conflict detection without a defined mechanism.
findings.evidence: Line 163 says only the AI-composition choice consumes agent tokens, but lines 169–173 promise detection of functional overlap and contradictory policy text. scripts/catalog_core.py:1–15 describes a static pattern-matching scanner; the cited evidence does not establish a general semantic conflict detector.
findings.fix: Limit the free path to concrete structural conflicts and declared overlap metadata. Make semantic analysis an explicitly optional agent operation rather than an unconditional installation guarantee.

findings.claim: X2 does not define the standard treatment it tests, and its replacement rule lacks a complete safety condition.
findings.evidence: Line 107 defines standard as reviewing a code diff and tests, while X2 supplies design documents. X2 allows S to replace E based on detection equivalence and cost without explicitly requiring S's false-positive safety. The fallback at line 264 also switches deep to S when E fails to generalize, without requiring an acceptable S-versus-N result.
findings.fix: Define the exact standard design-review treatment and distinguish it from code review. Give the replacement decision explicit quality and false-positive requirements, plus a deterministic fallback when neither treatment qualifies.

findings.claim: The specified add flow contradicts its one-question usability acceptance criterion.
findings.evidence: Line 165 requires the composition question, and line 176 then requires another tasting question for untested skills. Line 193 nevertheless requires completing add A B C, choosing option 1 and removing B while answering only one question.
findings.fix: Include optional tasting in the initial interaction or defer it without another installation prompt. Make the usability fixture explicitly contain untested skills.

findings.claim: The simplified map output omits an existing uncertainty distinction that matters for impact analysis.
findings.evidence: scripts/code_index.py:1540–1549 separates resolved callers from same-name calls with unknown receiver types, and lines 1733–1734 print a warning. Its traversal also has language and hop limits at lines 1577–1596. An untruncated result is not necessarily an exhaustive set of actual callers.
findings.fix: Preserve resolution warnings and state that 'complete' refers to returned indexed matches, with the applicable language and traversal limits.

findings.claim: The statement that all three maps reduced tool calls to 0.23–0.65 of native overstates the measurements.
findings.evidence: evidence/codemap-comparison-2026-11-06.md:28–40 reports graphify ratios of 0.88, 0.76, 1.00 and 1.04, and an OAW ratio of 1.04 on Opus 4.8. The 0.23 result is codegraph's separate VS Code experiment in evidence/validation-2026-11-07-RESULT.md:113. It is an overall tool-call ratio, not specifically a symbol-query measurement as attributed at plan line 131.
findings.fix: Report the ratios by tool and condition, and avoid attributing aggregate efficiency to an individually unmeasured mechanism.

findings.evidence: example/minimal-project/AGENTS.md:1–25 and the current rendered installer payload contain 25 lines, not 26. scripts/catalog.py:2512–2601 defines 23 top-level commands and four nested commands, not the 25 repeatedly claimed at plan lines 45 and 189.
findings.fix: Correct the counts and specify whether command counts include nested commands. Use the measured rendered policy as the line-count baseline.

findings.claim: The claimed TokenEconomizer failure caused by NFS clock skew is unsupported by the supplied evidence.
findings.evidence: evidence/codemap-comparison-2026-11-06.md:67 documents slow codegraph indexing on NFS, not clock skew or TokenEconomizer state failure. evidence/validation-2026-11-07-RESULT.md:30 and :54 discuss TokenEconomizer's ceiling results without that incident.
findings.fix: Supply the incident evidence or present local-cache placement as a design choice without claiming this measured cause.

questions: Which EGM preset and inputs will unattended deep review supply? The pinned workflow prompts when Step is omitted and can prompt for an ambiguous document split; its uninterrupted preset also writes reports, so the transition from plan-mode restrictions needs clarification.
What effort level and verification status will be reported when the in-session effort spike fails, given the proposed nonblocking fallback?
Will the new doctor checks inspect actual host discovery and enabled tools through a live probe, and report unknown when that probe is unavailable?
Does the approximately 23M Claude budget cover only experiments and reviews, or also implementation and repair work described as nearly zero-token?
summary: The plan addresses the owner's requested review flow, built-in EGM, code map, absorption SOP and three-choice skill interface, and most headline measurements match the evidence. It needs revisions to its statistical design, catalog integration, review timing and installation lifecycle before its acceptance rules and user-facing promises are executable.
